newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar corrects lower, arbitrage active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar corrects lower, arbitrage active.

text.p: London's white sugar futures market saw a continued downward correction after the recent dizzy rally as a mixed bag of sellers piled into the May contract and took profits, traders said on Thursday.
Both the whites and the raws markets corrected lower after a late fund-led buying spree pushed March raws up 33 points to 11.27 cents/lb and May whites up $4.80 to $312.30.
Both contracts closed at the highs. But the sudden strength lured sellers eager to take profits, so even with a slightly firmer London open basis May, the spot value quickly moved lower.
New York followed the same pattern and just compounded the London weakness, traders said. "We're just seeing it being given back again, the same way that New York has given back," said one.
"The whites are essentially following New York at the moment ...a lot of it is being done on arbitrage."
Commission houses were said to be active among the sellers and activity was concentrated in May, which at 1750 GMT stood $2.00 down at $310.30, off the $309.10 low.
August was $2.10 weaker at $309.90 and overall volume totalled 1,626 lots.

Traders were still awaiting the results of Iran's recent tender to buy white and raw sugar but noted the high futures prices could have prompted Iran to postpone until it could obtain sugar more cheaply.
Iraq issued a tender for February 25 to buy 120,000 tonnes of white sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
